stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, Public Law 88-452; quotations are from the act.
stimulus.text:
Paraphrase of the Economic Opportunity Act, signed August 20, 1964. The act said it was the policy of the United States "to eliminate the paradox of poverty in the midst of plenty" by opening to everyone "the opportunity for education and training, the opportunity to work, and the opportunity to live in decency and dignity."

It created the Office of Economic Opportunity to run new programs: the Job Corps, which gave young people ages 16 to 21 education and job training at residential centers; Volunteers in Service to America (VISTA), which sent volunteers to help poor communities; and community action programs, run "with the maximum feasible participation" of residents.

rationales.A: The phrase gives residents a part in running the programs, so Washington does not run them alone.
rationales.B: The phrase gives residents a part in the programs, so it lets them in, not keeps them out.
rationales.C: The phrase puts residents into the programs; it does not replace local government with federal officials.
rationales.D: The phrase says community action programs are run with the fullest workable part taken by the residents served.
rationales.general:
1. The phrase names the people who take part: the residents of the areas served.
2. 'Maximum feasible' means as much as can be worked out in practice.
3. Participation means taking part in running the program, not only receiving its help.
4. The programs were therefore meant to let the people served help run them.
Remember: Who takes part tells you who holds the power.
